#4357. Jordan Esports Federation signs MoU with King Hussein Business Park to host more events

Priya Venkatesh has been following the money in esports since before brand deals were considered legitimate marketing. She got pulled into the scene through competitive fighting games and eventually found herself more interested in the contracts and partnerships behind the tournaments than the matches themselves. These days she focuses on how brands navigate esports sponsorships, where the smart money is going, and which deals are actually built to last versus the ones that look good in a press release.

The Jordan Esports Federation (JEF) has signed a memorandum of understanding with King Hussein Business Park (KHBP) in Amman, giving the national body a formal framework to stage more tournaments and events at the site it already calls home.

KHBP announced the deal on Sunday in a statement published on its website. Prince Omar bin Faisal, who is President of the JEF, attended the signing.

Under the MoU, the federation and the business park will jointly host and organise specialised competitions on the KHBP campus. They will also receive the international delegations and official guests that travel to those events. Beyond the competitive side, the two organisations plan to cooperate on media and marketing, look at shared education, training and community projects, and swap knowledge and expertise.

Neither party has disclosed financial terms or the length of the agreement.

KHBP CEO Eng. Ammar Ezzeddin presented the MoU as part of the park’s wider ambitions. “This partnership builds on our ongoing efforts to create an enabling environment for institutions, initiatives and high-potential sectors, and to establish KHBP as a hub for innovation and technology,” he said.

He added: “We look forward to helping the sector thrive and to hosting more tournaments and events that put Jordanian talent in the spotlight and raise the Kingdom’s profile in this field.”

JEF Vice President Hazem Bawab focused on the competitive and grassroots goals. “This partnership is a significant step in our drive to develop the esports industry in Jordan and elevate the standard of local, regional and international competitions and activities,” he said.

Bawab continued: “We look forward to drawing on the setup and capabilities that KHBP offers to scale our work, nurture young talent and launch joint programmes that help the industry grow and encourage greater participation.”

The deal formalises a relationship that already exists on the ground. According to The Esports Radar, the JEF, which is the government recognised regulator for esports in the country, is based at the park in West Amman.

A lot of that work happens at THE ARC, the arena and gaming dome inside the park. The same report lists past events there including the fourth Arab Esports League, a Women’s Esports Championship and Red Bull Login, which doubled as Jordan’s national final stage in Dota 2 and Counter-Strike 2. The venue is also an incubation centre supported by the federation and the Ministry of Digital Economy and Entrepreneurship, and runs training camps for players hoping to turn professional.

KHBP has been a destination for esports investment for some time. In 2024, lounge operator True Gamers announced plans for an esports venue in Jordan at the business park, a project in which its CPO publicly thanked the JEF and Prince Omar.

The timing also puts Amman in the industry spotlight. PocketGamer.biz points out that Pocket Gamer Connects Jordan takes place on 7 and 8 November, bringing many of the region’s games industry stakeholders to the city later this week.

#4355. Nintendo Switch Sports Resort Review: Everything Switch Sports Should Have Been

Wuhu Island is back, and so is the magic. Nintendo Switch Sports Resort finally recaptures the charm that made me fall for this series years ago.

Say Nintendo Switch Sports Resort three times in a row. Go on, I’ll wait. It’s a tongue twister of a title, and I tripped over it every single time, which is at complete odds with the smoothness the game delivered.

The Nintendo DS didn’t just have great games, it had ideas that stuck around way longer than anyone expected.

I have played every entry in this series. When the Wii turned waving a remote around the living room into a whole new way of playing, I was right there, and I’ve had a soft spot for motion controls ever since. I do enjoy a good sports game, but if I’m honest, it’s mostly Nintendo’s that get me off the sofa. That’s also why I always worry a little whenever a new one is announced, because Nintendo Switch Sports never quite managed to feel like the series I fell in love with.

DualShockers was given a code for this review, and I’ve spent multiple hours on Wuhu Island so far, mostly in single player, on a docked Switch 2. I am nowhere near 100%, and I suspect that could take hundreds of hours depending on how good you are. But the hours I have put in have been more than enough to know this is the game I wanted Switch Sports to be.

The first thing I noticed was how little I was waiting. Load times are much shorter than in Nintendo Switch Sports, menus snap into place, and you can even rearrange the layout of the sports to suit you. Everything feels smoother, less clunky and quicker to get going. After the last entry, that alone felt like a small miracle.

Nintendo games always feel good, and I went in with high expectations of polish. Nintendo Switch Sports Resort met every single one of them. It ran perfectly on my docked Switch 2, and I didn’t run into a single bug or crash in my time playing this. Why can’t every game feel this polished?

My first birdie in Golf and my first strike in Bowling both made me grin like an idiot. It turns out the muscle memory I built up over years of these games is fully transferable, and it all just feels a bit more refined now. Bowling and Golf are still my favourites, Table Tennis gives you lovely control over every return, and Archery is so satisfying that I kept going back for “just one more” target. Tennis now comes with three courts to choose from, which is nice, if hardly a revolution.

Not everything landed quite as well. Boxing was the one I enjoyed least, because the Joy-Con 2 occasionally lost track of me once I mixed in ducks, hooks and jabs. Volleyball, unfortunately, still feels very sluggish, and that carries over into online play, too. It’s my single biggest deduction, and it’s a shame, because Volleyball also gave me one of my favourite moments.

Picture this: deuce after deuce, a match that seemingly will not end, my arms burning. By the time it was over, I was panting and had to sit down and rethink a few of my life choices. Nintendo, if you’re reading this, I desperately need a new Ring Fit Adventure, because that game actually kept me fit.

Then there’s Thumb Wrestling. It’s such an odd addition, and it makes me laugh every time, because it is so very Nintendo. It’s simple to pick up, there’s more strategy to it than you’d ever expect, and I can already see it causing chaos at parties. And yet.

I cannot believe they included Thumb Wrestling over my beloved Baseball. I’d have taken Disc Golf from the original Wii Sports Resort, too. Some of the racket and net sports also start to blur together after a while, so a little more variety would have gone a long way.

My favourite part of Resort is the trio of Leisure Sports, which have nothing to do with winning and everything to do with simply enjoying the island. Power Cruising puts you on a jet ski, with a Joy-Con held sideways like handlebars, twisting to accelerate and leaning to steer. Prop Plane turns your controller into a little aeroplane in your hand, and Skateboarding uses mouse mode, so you swipe across the table to push off and flick upwards for tricks. Luckily, the Nintendo Switch 2’s Welcome Tour trained me for exactly that moment. Generally, these sports are the most creative controls in the whole game, and they’re where I spent a lot of my down time.

Each of them comes with a Sightseeing Tour, where you have five minutes to explore and collect as much as you can. I’ll admit the timer sometimes had me wishing for more. There is a Free Roam mode without one, but none of the collectibles appear there, so it’s more of a scenic drive than a treasure hunt.

There’s no story in Resort, not really, but the sightseeing is the closest it gets. Finding photo spots and cruising past corners of Wuhu Island I’d never seen before taught me more about the place than any previous entry. It’s also the perfect palate cleanser after a sweaty round of Volleyball.

Hyrule has never looked better as they look in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake, and critics seem to agree!

Very quickly I discovered probably the number one reason that will keep me playing for months: everything counts now. In Nintendo Switch Sports, you could only earn the points needed to unlock new outfits and accessories by playing online. In Switch Sports Resort, every game you finish earns you points, single player included, and you spend them in a shop that rotates its collections weekly and monthly. You don’t even need a Nintendo Switch Online Membership anymore!

What you can pull from the shop is random and different for every user. It covers clothes, accessories, name tag options and sporting gear. On top of that, each sport has its own achievements, which you can unlock solo or with friends. As a bit of an achievement collector, that’s dangerous news for my free time.

For anyone who wants more of a challenge, Island Crown sets you up against increasingly skilled CPU players in each sport, with an Island Champ waiting at the top. The first few opponents are almost charmingly bad, but the tougher ones are genuinely tough. Nintendo has also added a little more “canon” this time, with each sport’s champion getting a bit of backstory. I haven’t beaten a single Champ yet, but I’m working on it.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort looks gorgeous. It’s bursting with colour and that typical Nintendo charm, and I never once got tired of looking at it. The soundtrack is upbeat and light-hearted, and returning players will recognise plenty of the sound cues. My favourite detail? In Golf, you can hear the waves crashing against the shore and birds chirping between your shots.

The island itself never feels empty. Miis stroll around in the background, and even the CPU opponents use the little stickers that are the game’s only way of communicating. You can play as the newer-style characters and the classic Miis, which made me happier than I’d like to admit. Every session left me feeling a little brighter, which is exactly what I want from this series.

Accessibility has taken a step forward, too. You can choose your dominant hand for every sport, turn on a colourblind mode, and switch off the emote pop-ups from other players and CPUs if you find them distracting. Golf has assistance options, and the tutorials are clear and helpful. You are still tied to the Joy-Cons and motion controls, though: there are no alternative control schemes, and nothing can be remapped.

This is a game for literally everyone. If you just want some fun, need something to play with your family or friends, or want an excuse to move a bit more, this game has you covered. You can play with one to four people locally, go online, take on CPU opponents, and even team up with a CPU partner in some sports. I can already see it becoming the focal point of many a games night.

What surprised me most is how good it is on your own. It’s the most fun I’ve had in a while, even playing completely alone. Games like this usually lose steam once the novelty wears off, but there’s so much variety here that I’m nowhere near running out of things to do.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort looks gorgeous. It’s bursting with colour and that typical Nintendo charm, and I never once got tired of looking at it.

Online play does have a couple of bumps in typical Nintendo fashion. Bowling has some strange waits between turns, and switching sports kicks you back to the lobby. These are pretty small complaints, though, when everything around them is this good. If anything, Nintendo has undersold this one: for how much better it is than its predecessor, it deserved a much bigger marketing push.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is a great revival for a series I’m always a little worried about. Nintendo is one of the only AAA players left that still brings real whimsy to the table, and Resort feels fresh, special, and complete from day one. If you want a sports game with actual substance, rather than a handful of minigames, this is the one. If you’d rather sink into a big story, look elsewhere – and if you hate fun? Honestly, I’m not sure how you ended up reading a review about Wii Sports' cheerful grandchild, but I admire the commitment. Somewhere on Wuhu Island, an Island Champ is waiting for me. I might not be ready yet. But I want to become the Island Legend, so I will keep training.

#4353. Battlefield 6's next season will speed up battle pass progression, and make it so Redsec players who don't own the game can actually make progress

Season 2 of Battlefield 6 looks to bring a host of broad, positive changes to XP, progression, audio and more.

Ahead of the start of Battlefield 6’s Season 2 next week, Battlefield Studios has shared some insight into a few of the major goals the developer has with the Season 2 patch. The game’s second season was delayed in mid-January, and the developer even brought back Battlefield Labs to test out some of the new content and features coming with the new season.

Indeed, the broader goals BF Studios shared with players in a new blog post reflect some of what Labs players already went hands-on with, while others are the result of work on long-standing issues with both the game itself, as well as free-to-play mode Redsec.

We know that Season 2 is introducing a big new map to the game, Contaminated, which the developer has been teasing. The map will indeed arrive in the first part of the season, and it’s going to do so alongside a new LTM that “introduces a new element of tactics.” A second, “high-intensity map” will debut later into the season, alongside another LTM where players battle through an underground base, in darkness.

The real meat of the blog post, however, covers the broader gameplay changes everyone will see once the new season kicks off. There’s a massive focus on player progression, especially when it concerns free-to-play Redsec players.

Challenges are being streamlined yet again, with more broad parameters that don’t require specific modes. Some, like dailies, will also allow for assists to count towards their criteria. Less restrictive challenges are welcome, but even more so is the faster battle pass progression.

BF Studios is changing the rate at which battle pass Tokens are earned from career XP, and making it so they’re earnable by playing the game normally, and by completing weekly challenges. These changes should also help Redsec players, who will also benefit from faster career and weapon XP earn rates - across both battle royale, and Gauntlet. In general, the career experience should feel more rewarding, especially for earlier ranks.

Weapon balance and recoil are two areas that will continue to evolve in Battlefield 6, it seems, and Season 2 is specifically tackling recoil patterns to make them more consistent when you compensate for them.

Movement is being adjusted with the Season 2 patch, too, though thankfully it’s limited to general feel that touches areas like vaulting, ladder transitions, and acceleration curves. You should also see better continuity and consistency between animations and feel.

Audio is getting a pass with the upcoming patch, especially when it comes to footstep and interaction audio. This also extends to something the developer has been working on improving for a while, and it has to do with how the game decides which audio tracks to prioritise in busy situations.

Tomorrow, the full Battlefield 6 Season 2 trailer will be released, while a more detailed roadmap is expected by the end of this week.

#4352. KRÜ Blaze win Game Changers Championship from lower bracket, ending Gentle Mates’ unbeaten run

KRÜ Blaze came through the lower bracket to beat Europe's Gentle Mates GC over five maps in São Paulo, giving LATAM its first Game Changers Championship title. They are also the last winners of the standalone event, as next year's final moves to Champions.

KRÜ Blaze are the 2026 VALORANT Game Changers Championship winners. They edged Gentle Mates GC 3-2 at the Riot Games Arena in São Paulo on 1 November. No Latin American team had lifted the title before. No team had ever won it from the lower bracket either.

The event ran from 22 October, with 10 teams competing. Gentle Mates earned US$100,000 as runners-up. Shopify Rebellion Gold took US$70,000 for third place and MIBR GC US$50,000 for fourth.

KRÜ took the long route. They beat Gen.G GC 2-1 in the upper-bracket quarter-finals on 23 October. A 2-0 loss to Shopify Rebellion Gold on 27 October then dropped them into the lower bracket. They answered with clean sweeps of Team Liquid Brazil and MIBR GC. On 31 October they beat Shopify Rebellion Gold 3-1 in the best-of-five lower-bracket final.

The grand final swung back and forth. Gentle Mates took Haven 13-5 before KRÜ levelled on Abyss by the same score. KRÜ led the third map 10-2 at half-time. Gentle Mates fought back, but KRÜ closed it out 14-12 in overtime. Gentle Mates then won Split 13-8 to force a decider. KRÜ led 11-5 on Ascent and won it by the same margin as Split.

Liquipedia named KRÜ’s Argentine player tok1o as the event’s MVP. Brazilian teammates antG and none became the first Brazilians to win an international tournament held in São Paulo.

The result breaks a pattern. Before 2026 the title went to G2 Gozen for Europe in 2022, Shopify Rebellion for North America in 2023 and 2024, and Team Liquid Brazil in 2025. KRÜ’s own record at the event had improved steadily. They finished 7th–8th in 2022 and 5th–6th in each of the next two years. Last year they came fourth.

For European fans, it was a painful near miss. Gentle Mates GC arrived as EMEA’s top seed on circuit points. The team had not lost a series in São Paulo before the final, according to Esports News UK.

It capped a strong debut season in the circuit. Gentle Mates won EMEA Stage 1 by sweeping G2 Gozen 3-0 on 22 February. They lost the Stage 2 final to SK Nebula on 24 May without winning a map. On 30 August they lost the Stage 3 final to G2 Gozen in a fifth map. Silver in São Paulo leaves them with one title from four finals this year.

After a lower bracket run in São Paulo, the LATAM squad claimed the #VCTGameChangers Championship trophy! pic.twitter.com/YeSeb10TZc

— VCT Pacific (@vctpacific) November 1, 2026

The São Paulo final also closes a format. KRÜ are the last team to lift the trophy at a separate event of its own. For the first time, the Game Changers Championship will finish at Champions. Under Riot’s 2027 plan, non-partner teams that qualify for the Game Changers Championship will receive an extra US0,000 incentive. VALORANT Champions 2027 is scheduled for 16 September to 10 October in Austin.

#4350. Diablo 4’s next class is the Warlock, but you can sort of play it today in Diablo 2: Resurrected’s new DLC

Blizzard has officially unveiled the Warlock, the second class coming to Diablo 4 with Lord of Hatred.

Diablo 4’s segment in the big Diablo 30th Anniversary Spotlight was among the biggest, even if the reason most of us tuned in was somewhat spoiled earlier in the same livestream. Blizzard unveiled the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The first class, being the Paladin, is already available to play for anyone who pre-ordered the expansion, but the Warlock won’t be accessible until the expansion arrives in late April.

The Warlocks are positioned as the opposite of the Paladins, in that they don’t mind utilising forbidden knowledge, drawing on the powers of Hell itself to fight its own overlords. The Warlock is the edgy, antihero counterpart to the Paladin’s purity and devotion to the Light.

The livestream did not show off any Warlock gameplay, but Blizzard is planning a dedicated livestream to show off the new class’ gameplay, and dig deeper into its lore and abilities. That show is scheduled for March 5.

What we did get to see was our first look at Skovos, the expansion’s new region. This Mediterranean-inspired location is where the new story arc will unfold, but it’s also being positioned as the endgame destination for Diablo 4 once the credits roll.

Lord of Hatred, of course, as previously revealed, introduces two new endgame modes in War Plans, and Echoing Hatred.

War Plans lets you create a custom playlist of up to five endgame activities to target specific rewards and create your own experience. There’s a new activity tree that works with all endgame activities, and creating War Plans is how you earn progression there.

Echoing Hatred, on the other hand, is a rare event that pits you against legions of Mephisto’s minions. It’s triggered through a rare lootable item that unlocks access. It’s essentially horde mode; where you’ll face unending waves of enemies, though not without a couple of twists.

We also got a bit more colour on the expanded class skill trees, which all players will benefit from when the expansion arrives. The Talisman system, which unlocks set bonuses, was also shown off. And, of course, the return of the iconic Horadric Cube, which gives you control over Affixes.

The Anniversary Spotlight should’ve had a Year of the Warlock subtitle, because the class is also making its way to both Diablo Immortal, as well as Diablo 2: Resurrected. The showcase revealed the Reign of the Warlock DLC, which adds the aforementioned Warlock to D2R - its first new class in 25 years.

Reign of the Warlock, which is available now in D2R, also makes a few updates to the game, such as new quality of life features, the Colossal Ancients endgame encounter, updated Terror Zones and more. You also get some cosmetics in Diablo 4 if you purchase this expansion.

#4344. You're not crazy, trying to heal in Nioh 3 sometimes doesn't work - and Team Ninja is fixing it

One of the more insidiously aggravating bugs in Nioh 3 makes it so the game ignores you when you try to use elixirs, but hopefully not for long.

Nioh 3 has received a hot new update that brings plenty of bug fixes to very specific issues, but it also implements fixes for a few of the most common - and incredibly annoying - bugs. Patch 1.03.01 arrived earlier on all platforms, and it comes with a chunky set of notes.

This latest update, predictably, doesn’t add any gameplay features, but some of the included fixes will absolutely delight - or vindicate - so many of the game’s millions of players.

There’s plenty to go through in the patch notes published today for update 1.03.01, but the most impactful is a fix for an issue that “sometimes made it impossible to use elixirs during battle.” This is only a partial fix, but if you ran into the problem of smashing that shortcut button and not seeing your character play the healing animation, you’ll be glad to see it.

This is a problem myself and others have faced, especially in boss fights. You can even see the shortcut register your button press and proceed to ignore you. Another partial fix has been made to an issue that caused the game to crash. Team Ninja didn’t share specifics on that, and though Nioh 3 has been fairly stable for me in 70+ hours, it has definitely crashed a few times.

If you’ve been playing since launch, you likely have - or know someone who has - run into issues with save file corruption and other weird bugs around certain trackable items within save files.

Team Ninja already rolled out a couple of fixes there, and this latest one specifically targets losing valuables during Myths. If your save file has been affected, the game will now check and recover what was lost. Even more interesting is that the game will now automatically create a backup copy of your save data any time you load a save.

If you’ve made it into the Eternal Rift, you’ll be happy to know that today’s update takes care of a few progression blockers, and fixes an issue that allowed some players to obtain certain items before they were supposed to, locking themselves out.

One of the more amusing fixes concerns Mujina, who had a tendency to respawn if you prayed at a Shrine after opening a chest it was hiding in, which made it appear far more often than a mimic should.

Finally, there’s a set of fixes that address bugs (and exploits) when using specific Martial Art with certain weapons. There are a few fixes to AI, Myths, and one problem with the Minamoto no Yoritomo boss fight that made it impossible to interrupt him, even after he runs out of Ki.

Hit the link at the top for the full change log, and check out our Nioh 3 gameplay tips if you haven’t already. You should also change these settings ASAP, as they’re going to make your life much easier and save you a lot of time.

#4343. Gen.G sweep LYON to end North America’s Worlds 2026 run and set up iG semi-final

Gen.G beat LYON 3-0 in Allen, Texas, removing North America's last team from Worlds 2026. The LCK top seed are now one series from a first Worlds final, with a revived Invictus Gaming in the way.

Gen.G swept LYON in the second Worlds 2026 quarter-final in Allen, Texas. The defeat removes North America’s last team from the tournament. The LCK top seed now face Invictus Gaming in a best-of-five semi-final on Saturday, starting at 16:00 Central Time.

Reaching the last four secures Gen.G at least third or fourth place. That is a familiar stopping point for the organisation. It has finished third or fourth at four of its last five Worlds and has never played in a Worlds final, GosuGamers reported.

The stakes go beyond one team. Gen.G entered the tournament as the LCK’s top seed. Korean sides are chasing a fifth Summoner’s Cup in a row.

Their opponents bring their own history. Invictus Gaming beat Top Esports 3-1 in the opening quarter-final. That put iG into their first Worlds semi-final since 2019. TheShy and Rookie, who won Worlds with iG in 2018, are back in the last four.

The money rises sharply from here. Worlds 2026 carries a US$5,000,000 prize pool. The champion takes US$1,000,000 (20%), and the runner-up receives US$800,000.

For LYON, the exit still marks clear progress. They go out in joint fifth to eighth place and collect a share of the prize money. GosuGamers called it easily the organisation’s best Worlds finish. In four earlier appearances, LYON never placed higher than 17th.

Their elimination also changes the shape of the event. North America will have no representative in the semi-finals or the Grand Final. The remaining matches in Allen will be contested without a team from the region.

Genshin Impact's next update will have you reminiscing about the good ol' days of... 2020.

The latest big content update has been revealed for HoYoverse's breakout game, Genshin Impact. Version Luna 5, which has the unusually long and needlessly layered title — Song of the Welkin Moon: Variation - Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind — is set to arrive February 25.

This one is a bit of a nostalgia play, taking everyone back to Mondstadt, the place where you may remember taking your first steps. And, as with any good return to the ol’ hunting grounds, come familiar characters, too.

The big new arrival is Varka, who joins as a playable character for the first time. Varka, Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius, is a character whose debut has been long-awaited. He is a 5-Star Anemo Claymore wielder with a dual-wield combat style, capable of dealing two different types of Elemental damage. His addition means that there's now finally a burly 5-Star male character of each elemental type... do with that information what you will.

Varka's dual-wielding combat style allows him to deal two different types of Elemental damage at the same time. The way it works is that his Elemental Skill boosts the damage of his regular attacks, but it also converts the damage type of his right-hand claymore to match his teammates’ elements (Pyro, Hydro, Electro, or Cryo). The left-hand claymore always deals Anemo damage.

The more normal attacks you use, the more frequently he can activate a special Elemental Skill, or trigger a Charged Attack that doesn’t consume stamina. He can also rely on the Hexerei effect to trigger more instances of Elemental Skill, as well as Charged Attacks, making him a monster damage-dealer.

Varka, of course, has been a staple member of the cast, featuring in both the original story in a small cameo, as well as taking a bigger role in the recent Nod-Krai chapters. With the return to Mondstadt, his playable debut makes sense. His Story Quest will shed light on his encounter with the Wild Hunt, and the Great Wolf King of the North

The reruns for this version are going to be Flins — who will be available in the first phase of Event Wishes — as well as Skirk and Escoffier in the second phase. You can also look forward to the return of the Chronicled Wish with Mondstadt characters.

Staying on the theme of reminiscence, the big event in Luna 5 is centered around revisiting memories from the beginning of your time with Genshin Impact, and reuniting with old friends. In Echoes of Memory, you’ll witness familiar scenes that have been changed slightly, and you’ll need to use the Spotter Kamera to detect and record those differences.

The Knights of Favonius are hosting several other activities for everyone to take part in, including an event that lets you catch up with old friends over drinks which you make for them.

Outside of events, there’s a new set of Gliding and Combat Challenges. And, of course, there are new minigames that you can relax with. The Kamera is being utilised yet again, and this time you can use to capture sights from your time in spots across Natlan, Fontaine, and Sumeru. There’s also… a horde mode of a sort, where you fend off waves of enemies.

#4340. Here's The Best Graphics And Performance Mode For Phantom Blade Zero On PlayStation 5

Phantom Blade Zero is out now for everyone as a console exclusive on PlayStation 5 and on PC via Steam and the Epic Games Store as well. If you missed it, it's my favorite action game of the year so far, and you can read why in Game Informer's Phantom Blade Zero review. That explains why I think you should check the game out; Game Informer's list of Phantom Blade Zero tips and tricks will get you some key information I wish I had when I started the game; and this guide I wrote up about the requirements you need to get the best ending in Phantom Blade Zero will help you find all story-critical content in the game.

However, you're looking for advice on which of the three visual modes Phantom Blade Zero offers you should use on your PS5. This here piece is for you.

Phantom Blade Zero has three visual modes on PS5 Pro: Quality, Balanced, and Performance. I tested all three. My personal favorite was Balanced, which gives you an upscaled (checkerboarded) 4K resolution at 40 FPS, as long as you have a 120Hz TV with VRR. If you have a 120Hz TV, it likely has VRR because most major manufacturers include it with 120Hz. I like this mode because the upscaled 4K looks beautiful, just a hair less than native 4K, and if you aren't someone super trained on those details, I'd wager you won't notice the difference. The best part is that this mode offers 40 FPS gameplay, which, contrary to how math works, is halfway between 30 FPS and 60 FPS; I'm not kidding, look it up. As such, 40 FPS feels much smoother than 30 FPS, and you're still getting crisp 4K resolution. It's a win-win for me and my go-to mode when a game offers it. That said, if you don’t have a PS5 Pro, you won’t see this Balanced mode.

The Performance mode offers an upscaled 2K resolution with a pretty locked 60 FPS. Phantom Blade Zero is an extremely fast, fluid action game, so I think many people will want the buttery smoothness of 60 FPS gameplay. If that's you, pick the Performance mode. Sure, its resolution is lower, and it will look blurrier and less crisp than the other two modes, but if you aren't switching back and forth often or looking at side-by-side images, you likely won't notice.

Quality mode is native 4K resolution (absolutely beautiful, the best visual image you can get playing Phantom Blade Zero), but at 30 FPS... and for a game like this, I don't think 30 FPS does it justice. I don't really recommend this mode for combat, but if you're just waltzing around Wulin, grabbing screenshots and such, turn it on and bask in the wonders of developer S-Game's art team. Note: There is an option for ray tracing on PS5 Pro. I tested all three graphics modes with it on and off and noticed zero performance changes or issues. So, use ray tracing – it’s nice!

#4339. The Ratchet & Clank Game You Didn’t Know Existed is Shutting Down

Daniel is a lifelong gamer with a love for various genres and gameplay styles who enjoys exploring games and playing from various angles.

I’ll admit, I have a tendency to hyperfixate on games and franchises that I care about, occasionally to the detriment of others. Even so, I like to consider myself sufficiently plugged-into this industry, especially when it comes to relatively big-name IPs like the Ratchet & Clank series. You can imagine my distinct confusion, then, when I heard today that Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble was shutting down, to which my response was, “what the heck is Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble?”

Apparently it is, soon to be “was,” a PvP live service shooter available for iOS and Android. The game saw a soft-launch in mid-2025 in limited territories like Canada, France, and parts of Asia, which probably explains why I have literally never heard of it alongside the fact that I don’t often pay much mind to mobile games in general.

In the wake of Destiny 2's upcoming final content update, thousands of of fans have called for Destiny 3 to begin development.

What’s especially interesting about this particular discontinuation, however, is that the game wasn’t even actually finished yet. That soft-launch was as far as the game had ever managed to get, with its planned global launch officially being scrapped and further development ceasing as of the game’s most recent update today, according to its official home page.

As the home page announcement explains, with the newest update pushed out today to mobile storefronts, no further updates for Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble will be released, and on November 21, the game will be pulled from said storefronts entirely.

This is a feature that looks at how live service games are dying as a popular choice in the industry.

For those who are still actively playing the game, you don’t have to stop playing it right away. While new players won’t be able to download the game from the Google Play or Apple App stores anymore following the delisting, anyone who already has the game downloaded will be able to keep playing multiplayer matches until the servers are officially closed in May 2027.

On November 21, the game will be pulled from storefronts entirely.

The game’s “Qwark Pass” seasons will continue running until the server closure, while the game’s “Super Pass” has been made free, with all of its related content now available to earn throughout the remaining seasons. Of course, said content will vanish into the ether once the game goes offline, so whether or not you can be bothered is up to you.

This also goes for any in-app purchases made on things like currency, cosmetics, upgrades, and so forth. If you’re looking to get a refund for any of that, the developers suggest you contact the Apple App Store and Google Play Store’s respective support lines to determine eligibility. Again, absolutely everything is being erased when the servers shutter in May, so whether you want a refund or to keep playing, you’d better act now.

In its final announcement, the developers offered some words of thanks to the players who joined them for the soft-launch process. “On behalf of the dev team and everyone helping to make the game, thanks to our amazing community for all your support, especially to those who have spent time playing, sharing feedback, and helping shape Ranger Rumble throughout its development,” they wrote.

While not as high-profile as some other historic live-service flops over the years, the discontinuation of Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble is another good sign that live-service games are reaching the end of an era. Aside from a very fortunate few that manage to keep attention with consistent updates and player-grabbing content like Fortnite’s One Piece event, the majority end up crashing and burning well before they can take off in earnest.

Sony in particular has been putting the kibosh on live-service games left and right for the last couple of years, mostly following the disastrous launch of Concord, and it seems even its major first-party PlayStation IPs like Ratchet & Clank aren’t safe from the proverbial axe.

Sony Interactive Entertainment executive Hideaki Nishino doubles down on multiplayer investments during a recent Famitsu interview.

#4334. The Sims 4 developer hasn't forgotten about its quality of life commitment, and is back with an update on what to expect in 2026

Maxis has offered some fresh details on its long-running mission to improve player quality of life in The Sims 4.

As the The Sims 4 continues into its second decade, the volume of new content, major expansions, and long-awaited features has grown in lockstep. Unfortunately, that has also meant that, given how old the game is, a few technical problems remain a nuisance.

The effort required to fix them is what led developer Maxis to make a commitment to improve the game’s technical state, and the developer has now returned to update the community on what to expect in 2026.

The quality of life pledge was made in September last year, through the introduction of a roadmap. Since then, the developer issued one update on its progress. Which brings us to this week’s new blog post, which further builds on everything that’s come before.

In the post, Maxis revealed a few key areas it’s going to be focusing on going forward. Though specific release dates for these changes were not shared, the list of issues should resonate with many players, as it covers many often-discussed topics.

The first stage of the new roadmap covers March through August. Over that period, you can expect Sims' autonomy to improve. This goes for things like how they choose locations for certain actions, they way they interact with certain objects, and even how often they interrupt conversations.

The infant and caregiver relationship is being updated, too, in order to improve autonomy and make sure your little Sims don’t miss out on milestones and interactions. That stage of the roadmap also includes fixes for black photo issues, and other crashes and freezing.

The next period takes place September through December, and it includes more interesting changes. One of the goals with this one is to improve Sims’ dining experience, which covers issues around eating and drinking.

Another important area of focus with this stage is family trees, and relationships between members of the same family. Maxis wants to improve the game’s genealogy systems to make relationship tracking across generations more robust so that your family history isn’t lost.

Depending on how the first stage goes, you might see more issues join the list of what the developer is looking at for the second stage of the roadmap.

The good news is that you won’t have to wait too long for the game’s next patch. Due out in March, this next update will feature around 55 fixes, including for some commonly reported issues.

Until then, you may want to check out The Sims 4’s Lost Legacies Event, which is available now until the middle of March. If you picked up the game’s latest expansion, check if you tried those Royalty & Legacy cheats.

#4331. Genshin Impact fans on PS4 only have six weeks to find another platform as support winds down with one final update

Premium in-game purchases have now been disabled on PlayStation 4, as one of Genshin's four original launch platforms prepares to get dropped in early April.

Version Luna 5 of Genshin Impact is now live, but it's a bittersweet occasion for fans of HoYoverse's breakout gacha RPG – at the very least, those who are still playing the game on PlayStation 4, which is presumably true of somebody out there.

HoYoverse announced last year that they intended to wind down support for Genshin Impact on PS4, which – alongside PC, Android, and iOS – was one of the launch platforms for the game back in 2020. And with Version Luna 5, those end days are upon us.

The game has already been delisted on the platform since last September, meaning it was no longer available for download and could only be updated by players who already had it installed. But as of today, paid purchases from the in-game store have been disabled on PS4; and in six weeks' time, on approximately April 8, Version Luna 6 will discontinue access to the PS4 version altogether.

In many ways this is unsurprising – Genshin is already available on both PS5 and Xbox Series to sate fans eager to play on console, and the PS4's hardware is increasingly struggling to keep up with this massive open-world game after more than five years of regular updates have ballooned both its file size and technical requirements.

Aptly enough, Luna 5 takes the main story action back to the nation of Mondstadt, the location where the Traveler (and, by extension, the players) took their first steps into the world of Teyvat back in September 2020. It feels like a symbolic last hurrah for the original console home of the game, as does the inclusion of a Chronicled Wish banner focussing on some of Mondstadt's most iconic (read: too old to be meta by now) 5-Star characters – namely Eula, Mona, Albedo, Klee, Diluc, and Jean.

And as the icing on the Tea Break Pancake, this banner is running alongside the long-anticipated introduction of Varka – the Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius who has been a major character in the game's lore from the very beginning, but who only became playable with today's update.

Looking ahead to that post-Luna 6 future, Genshin Impact will still be available on PS5, as well as Xbox Series consoles, PC, and mobile devices – so hopefully anyone who is still playing primarily on PS4 will find another platform they can continue the adventure on by April.

#4330. What To Do If The Unlearn Button Is Missing In WoW: Forever

World of Warcraft: Forever lets you learn up to two primary professions at a time, but you aren't stuck with your first choice. Maybe you picked Mining and Herbalism to earn gold selling materials at the auction house while leveling, only to decide later you'd rather craft your own gear or potions.

Fortunately, you can unlearn a profession to make room for a new one. Before switching, though, it's worth knowing where to find the option and what happens to your progress. We also encountered an issue with the unlearn button, but found a workaround that fixed it for us.

You don't need to visit a trainer to unlearn a profession.

Once you confirm, that profession is removed, and its slot becomes available. You can then visit a profession trainer to learn a new profession.

However, unlearning a profession resets your skill progress and removes the recipes you've unlocked. If you take up that profession again later, your previous progress won't return automatically, and you'll have to relearn its recipes. This applies to both purchased and looted recipes.

Only primary professions count toward the two-profession limit. Cooking, Fishing, and First Aid are secondary professions, and you can learn all three without using either primary slot.

A World of Warcraft Forever player has taken matters into their own hands after the flood of new Olympus guilds overseen by Asmongold.

We encountered an issue where the red X appeared as a blank space in the Professions window. The Unlearn tooltip appeared next to the blank space when we hovered over it, but we couldn't click the button. Changing the UI Scale in our game fixed the issue and let us unlearn professions again.

Unlearning a profession in World of Warcraft: Forever only takes a few steps, and adjusting the UI Scale may help if the red X isn't appearing. Just double-check your choice before confirming. You can always learn the profession again, but your previous skill progress and recipes won't automatically return.

There's another free-to-play action RPG very much on the horizon. Will this be the one to win you over?

It seems like we’re getting one of these every few months, but the world of mobile action RPGs that look like the games that, just a few years back, were only possible on consoles is expanding with another new entry.

Netmarble, a studio and publisher known for its free-to-play games on mobile and PC, recently unveiled the launch date for The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin, its next major release that’s very much coming for the Genshin Impact crowd.

The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin is an open-world action RPG based on the world of The Seven Deadly Sins anime and manga. The game takes place in the world of Britannia, which looks similar to the way it does in the anime.

That said, the story of the game is not based on the anime or manga, Instead, it’s an original story set in the universe of the show. You play as Prince Tristan of the Kingdom of Liones who must find a way to bring order back to Britannia.

The gameplay should be familiar to anyone who played a free-to-play action RPG in the last decade. It features action combat, a roster of diverse heroes that you assemble to form teams, and a large pretty world to explore where you’ll also get to meet new characters.

Speaking of which, while Origin has its own original story, expect to be teaming up with characters from the series - some of whom wouldn't be able to meet naturally. You can thank the game's multiversal story for that.

Beyond all the serious business of saving the world and battling monsters, The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin also has a cozy, relaxing side. You’ll be able to fish, cook, forage and take on the beauty of the world with your pals.

The game has a bit of an unusual release schedule. It’s set to arrive on PC, PS5, iOS, and Android. PC (Steam), and PS5 players will be able to jump in starting March 16, whereas the global mobile launch is scheduled for one week later, on March 23.

You can pre-register right now on the official website if you’re interested in earning a few rewards when the game launches. You can, of course, always wishlist the game on Steam and the PlayStation Store, too.

In terms of current games, Assassin’s Creed Valhalla is getting a long-requested New Game Plus thanks to a new update coming on November 5. This means you can start a fresh game while bringing over your progression items/level from your previous playthrough. This update will also introduce the following features:

#4326. 8 Best Anime Where Tiny Details Become Major Story Revelations

Usama Mehmood is a Senior Writer at DualShockers with more than five years of experience in the video game industry. He has been writing professionally since 2021 and covering games since 2022, with work spanning guides, lists, reviews, and features across action-adventure games, JRPGs, open-world titles, racing games,

You know, I’ve rewatched certain anime scenes more times than I’d like to admit on YT or just browsing social media, and it's almost never for the big moments. It’s usually for something small: a character’s hand hovering a half-second too long or a line of dialogue that sounded like filler. Then, twenty episodes later, the show unexpectedly turns that one detail into the thing that rewrites almost everything you thought you knew about it.

Watched These Once? These 8 Anime Hit Harder the Second Time Around

It’s like that foreshadowing or missing puzzle piece coming back later that just makes you bewildered for a second or two at the show’s ingenious attention-to-detail, or, well, certain parts of it, to be exact. It made rewatches feel like detective work, and it also makes you appreciate how much patience and planning go into a story that pays off its smallest choices.

So this anime list is for the shows that reward that kind of attention, especially the ones where you can catch the smallest details and understand why they become so prevalent later, during the climax. Naturally, there are lots of spoilers ahead for the discussed anime, so watch out!

It’s funny that I recommended this show to a friend who went into Higurashi expecting a wholesome slice-of-life show, only to regret trusting my recommendation. It's a horror show that takes some characters’ quirks and uses them as pivotal anchors in later episodes.

Take the first arc, for instance: when Keiichi starts scratching his throat, you get the impression that it's a nervous habit. A few arcs later, you realize it’s the first symptom of the Hinamizawa Syndrome, which explains why people who were perfectly friendly suddenly turn on each other.

The twins are another example. See, you know Mion and Shion Sonozaki look nearly identical, and the show plays with that on purpose, but once you know how the identity swap works, you start to doubt every earlier scene where “Mion” seemed slightly off. I can get why some people think this show is straight-up torture, but don’t knock it till you try, am I right?

Let me preface this by saying we don’t argue between Aronofsky’s Black Swan and Satoshi Kon’s Perfect Blue; I love both. This cult-favorite anime movie’s best trick is how it plays with your sense of what’s real. Mima’s decision to quit her pop group CHAM! and become an actress feels like a simple career move, but as you watch, the film shows how every “step forward” she takes strips away a piece of her.

The tiny, uneasy moments, like her flinching at the fax of the Double Bind script or the way her reflection starts reacting a half-beat late, are the film silently telling you that Mima isn’t in control of her own image anymore. And that’s one of the key reasons I adore this movie, even after all these years since I first watched it.

These anime plot twists flipped entire stories on their heads.

On a first watch, Madoka Magica looks like a bright, pastel magical girl series… until you rewatch it and realize it was telling you exactly how it would break your heart from the very first episode. Almost everything in the show, from the unusual designs of the Witch's Labyrinths to the seemingly innocent conversations with Kyubey, carries far more meaning than it initially lets on to you.

I mean, for crying out loud, the show's opening, with its seemingly disconnected imagery and Madoka chasing after a mysterious figure, becomes much more meaningful once you understand what's really happening. Even small character choices carry weight. Mami’s tea parties, her loneliness, and her insistence on keeping up the cheerful senpai act are all easy to read as charm early on in this show.

Now I’ll be very real with you all here; Odd Taxi looks like a quiet slice-of-life show about a walrus cab driver named Hiroshi Odokawa, and it’s hard to say anything about it without spoiling it. He’s a dry, awkward man who talks in deadpan dad jokes and likes listening to a comedy podcast between fares.

Then a missing girl, a yakuza fixer, an idol group, a struggling comedian, and a nurse with a secret all begin orbiting his cab. What looks like a pile of unrelated conversations turns out to be a tightly built puzzle, and almost every piece of it was planted in the very first episodes.

Early on, much of the dialogue feels like filler, with passengers rambling about their lives or Odokawa making small talk, until you later realize this throwaway stuff sets up most of the plot because a casual remark about a missing person, an offhand comment about someone’s job, or even a name dropped once in passing can fill in the main structure of the mystery. The show trusts you to notice, and it rewards you.

Dive into anime with controversial endings with modern shockers like Death Note and classics such as Evangelion.

Everyone knew this was going to be here, and it deserves it even if it's an obvious pick for this list. Death Note is an anime practically built around the idea that the smallest details can make the biggest difference.

What starts as a straightforward cat-and-mouse game between Light and L quickly becomes an elaborate battle of deduction, manipulation, and psychological warfare, where a seemingly insignificant action can expose someone's entire plan.

Whether it's L noticing the peculiarities of Kira's early killings or Light carefully manipulating the Death Note’s rules, the show constantly rewards those who pay attention. It's incredibly satisfying to watch everything click into place, and while the latter half isn’t everyone’s favorite for obvious reasons, the finale is genuinely one of the most memorable endings in the entire anime medium.

I might be biased for including this because Steins;Gate is genuinely one of my favorite anime of all time, and just a few months ago in August, I had the chance to review the Steins;Gate Reboot VN—and the entire thing was just as good as I remembered.

It starts as a quirky science-fiction adventure about a group of eccentric friends experimenting with a microwave, then accidentally stumbles into a conspiracy-theory time-travel adventure that gradually becomes one of the most intricately woven narratives in the medium. I know that sounds like a mouthful, but anyone who’s seen the show will know the series is just like that in terms of writing.

The genius is in how casually the show introduces certain characters, conversations, messages, and seemingly throwaway moments before revealing just how important they are to the bigger picture at the very end, or just when a certain pocket watch strikes 7:35 PM. Sorry, had to do it.

Look, we’re not even going to get into the debate about how the show ended, so this will focus strictly on Attack on Titan’s brilliant foreshadowing, which led to major story revelations and more twists, as my listicle’s title already suggests.

No matter what you think of his directional choices for the last act, Isayama has an incredible knack for planting seemingly insignificant details throughout the story. Things like the truth behind the Walls, the mystery surrounding Eren's basement, and the peculiar behavior of certain Titans initially seem like separate mysteries, but eventually come together in ways that completely change your understanding of the world in later seasons.

Even ordinary moments in both the manga and anime involving characters like Reiner, Bertholdt, and Annie become far more interesting once you pay attention to their behavior or dialogue, since they ultimately foreshadow their twists.

Naoki Urasawa is one of the most legendary manga auteurs with a wide range of back-to-back bangers under his umbrella, but his work in Monster is honestly one of the best things you’ll ever get to see, as long as you’re patient enough.

This slow-burn psychological thriller is the kind of story where an innocent conversation or a character's seemingly insignificant memory can carry far more weight than you initially realize. Even some of the twists thrown in here at times can recontextualize things you've already witnessed in previous episodes, making them feel completely different when you look back at them.

The mystery surrounding Johan, the Kinderheim 511 experiments, and the disturbing picture-book stories are all excellent examples of how Urasawa plants little breadcrumbs throughout the narrative before gradually revealing their significance.

From One Piece's grand treasure to Itachi's tragic illness, these unsolved anime mysteries leave fans guessing.

#4322. The Sims 4 is getting paid mods, and a new in-game currency to pay for them

The Sims 4 is about to launch a couple of major initiatives that may not exactly be what players have been looking for.

The Sims 4 has officially entered into its paid mods era. Developer Maxis announced The Sims Maker Program, and The Sims 4 Marketplace - two new destinations to publish, and discover new add-on content.

The two new features will arrive first on PC and Mac, starting March 17. PlayStation and Xbox players will receive them over the next couple of months, which is very much in line with how other franchises have rolled out their own paid mods systems.

The Maker Program is a way for community creators to get their work out there, and profit from it. The content they create will end up on the Marketplace, where other players can browse it, and pay for it if they want to use it in their game.

Created content will be available across all platforms. All previous packs The Sims 4 players should be familiar with will move to the Marketplace, too: once the feature launches, this is where you’re going to find Expansion Packs, Game Packs, Stuff Packs, Kits, and other official additions created by Maxis.

Alongside this, the game is also introducing a new virtual currency - Moola - which is what you’re going to use to purchase Maker Packs, as well as Sims 4 Kits in the Marketplace. A portion of your purchase will go to the creator (roughly 30%) of what you buy.

It is worth noting, however, that you’ll still be able to buy Expansion Packs, Game Packs, and Stuff Packs without having to purchase Moola, or go through the Marketplace. Kits are the only items that will no longer be available on the existing PC/console storefronts. Moola comes in the usual denominations you’ve seen a hundred items in other games’ in-game shops.

In order to start creating custom content and publishing it on the Marketplace, you’ll need to first be accepted into the program. Once that’s done, you’ll be able to directly publish your content on the Marketplace.

In the blog post announcing the new features, Maxis said that creators will have control over the price of their content, and how it's packaged. These are referred to as Maker Packs, which can include Create-a-Sim or Build/Buy items.

You can apply to become a Maker from March 5. Once accepted, you’ll also get access to the Maker Suite, which is what you’re going to use to test your work to ensure it runs smoothly on the different platforms, and eventually publish it.

#4320. Where To Hide Secondary Name In WoW: Forever

World of Warcraft: Forever introduces a two-part naming system, giving each character a main name and a secondary name. Rather than being unique to an individual realm, your full name must now be unique across your region.

This means you can still use a main name another player has already chosen, as long as the full two-part combination is available. But maybe you picked a random secondary name because you couldn't wait to see how your favorite starting area has changed since 2004. Luckily, you can control how that secondary name appears in-game.

Your secondary name appears above your character's head, in your character's portrait frame, and above your pet or minion. You can hide it from these UI elements if you'd prefer to see only your main name.

After unchecking the box, your secondary name will disappear from the affected displays immediately, without needing to restart the game. If you change your mind, return to the same menu and check the box again to restore it.

However, keep a couple of things in mind.

Your full character name will still appear in chat, even with the setting disabled. The setting also carries over between characters and rulesets. If you want to hide your secondary name on one character but show it on another, you'll need to change the setting each time you swap between your characters.

Pirate Software’s OnlyFangs raid controversy just got put on blast in a new WoW: Forever trailer.

In realm-based versions of World of Warcraft, players could use the same character name on different realms because names only needed to be unique within each realm. The new realmless structure removes that separation, making secondary names necessary to distinguish players who choose the same main name.

Think of secondary names like surnames. Two characters can share a main name as long as their full names differ. This flexibility is especially useful because numbers and symbols aren't supported in character names. Instead of changing the spelling of your favorite main name, you can pair it with a different secondary name. Keep in mind that Blizzard's standard naming rules still apply to both parts.

Whether you choose a meaningful surname or something random to get started, you don't have to keep it on display. Your full name remains intact, but how much of it you see is up to you.

#4316. EA Reportedly Closed BioWare To Invest In Developing Star Wars Battlefront III Instead Of The Next Mass Effect

Electronic Arts shut down the legendary RPG studio BioWare last week, ending development on an untitled fifth Mass Effect game. Since then, we've seen what appears to be a leaked trailer for the game, which suggests it might have been called Mass Effect Universe, and heard a sneak peek at what Grammy-winning composer Austin Wintory was cooking up for the beloved sci-fi RPG series. Over the past week, fans across the internet have tried to piece together how a publisher could decide to shut down a studio as prolific as BioWare, but according to a new Bloomberg report, the answer is Star Wars.

More specifically, Bloomberg writes that, presented with the opportunity to develop Star Wars Battlefront III with Disney, the publisher, which went private last year after a $55 billion acquisition,  chose to invest its money into that instead of BioWare's in-development Mass Effect sequel. The publication writes that EA looked at its portfolio for the coming years and had two massive sci-fi investments it could continue: Star Wars Battlefront III or BioWare's next Mass Effect. Even though Mass Effect was well into development, and even though the Battlefront threequel hasn't even entered development, EA chose to continue with the latter. And so BioWare was shut down, and Mass Effect development ended, though Bloomberg's sources say there are other, less significant reasons the studio was shuttered, too.

Those other factors include the poor reception to 2017's Mass Effect: Andromeda, the failure of Anthem in 2019, and 2024's Dragon Age: The Veilguard, which, despite garnering positive critical reception, apparently missed EA's sales expectations by 50%.

There's also the uncomfortable reality that BioWare made progressive LGBTQIA+ positive games but was a studio within a publisher house now partially owned by the Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia, a government fund from a country where same-sex activity, including marriage, is criminalized, sometimes punishable by death; these harsh laws extend to other facets of the LGBTQIA+ community. Another investment partner in this acquisition of EA is Affinity Partners, a Miami-based investment firm founded and run by former White House senior advisor Jared Kushner, who is the son-in-law of President Donald Trump, a political figure who imposes laws that discriminate against the LGBTQIA+ community, especially the 1% of Americans who are transgender; Trump has also been known to mock this community in various ways. No official statements say BioWare shut down because of its progressive leanings, but one has to wonder if that was a factor, especially after reports that BioWare scrubbed diversity from demos to avoid negative feedback from EA (thanks, Kotaku).

When BioWare closed last week, only 50 employees remained, all working on the next Mass Effect, after years of layoffs at the studio.

A Mass Effect TV series is still in the works at Amazon, even though EA seems to have hung up Commander Shepard's video game suit for good.

#4315. Diablo 4's next season is short, but it lets you become The Butcher, and it has Doom: The Dark Ages skins you probably can't afford

Blizzard has unveiled the next Diablo 4 season, which kicks off next week to hold us over until the launch of the game's big expansion in April.

The big Diablo 4 Developer Update has indeed delivered the goods. One of the livestream’s big topics was, of course, the game’s upcoming mini-season, which is set to kick off next week and run until the launch of Lord of Hatred, the game’s anticipated next expansion.

You can tell Blizzard wanted to have a bit of fun with Season of Slaughter, as many of its major features make it look like a limited-time event, but there is plenty to be excited about here.

Season of Slaughter kicks off March 11, and will run until the following season kicks off April 28, with the launch of the Lord of Hatred expansion. Many of the season’s biggest additions were available to preview in the 2.6.0 Public Test Realm.

Patch 2.6.0, as you might have guessed, is the one that will kick off the slaughter next week. The headline feature here is ability to become The Butcher, the iconic in-game boss who randomly invades players’ games.

When you play as The Butcher, you’ll be rewarded the more kills you get in quick succession. Your skills hotbar will transform to become something more fitting of The Butcher, making them more brutal. You’ll also earn a seasonal currency as you play.

Starting the seasonal questline is how you can begin to assume The Butcher’s form. A Taste of Power can be initiated from Gea Kul. Transforming into The Butcher can be done in a few ways. As you play, you’ll earn Meaty Offerings, which can later be spent on Shrines of Slaughter in the new Helltide. Once activated, the shrine will draw more enemies towards you.

If you never venture into PvP zones in Diablo 4, this season may change your mind. The standard PvP combat that could only be found in Fields of Hatred has been replaced with a Ceremony of Slaughter, a new event that rewards you for killing enemies quickly. See it through and The Butcher’s Idol will spawn, allowing you to transform into it.

Elsewhere in the world, you’ll also be able to attain the same power at Slaughterhouses, a new activity type available this season. Inside, you immediately become The Butcher for the entirety of the run.

The Butcher’s arrival also ties into two of the other Season of Slaughter’s more interesting additions. First, the Killstreak system finally arrives in Diablo 4, rewarding you for being as efficient as possible in carving your way through enemies.

Anyone who played Diablo 3 should be familiar with how it works. It kicks off the moment you get a kill, and has a visible timer where you’ll need continue performing the same action to up your streak. The more kills you get, the more often your timer will refresh.

There are five tiers to climb through: Killstreak, Carnage, Devastation, Bloodbath, and Massacre. You’re awarded for the tier you manage to reach before the timer runs out. You’ll earn XP and seasonal rep each time a Killstreak is achieved.

The other Butcher-themed addition is Bloodied Items, which is a new item quality available throughout this season. They play into the Killstreak system to grant you even more power. Bloodied Items come with unique affixes that scale off your Killstreak tier. You’ll see many familiar items in that pool, as any item in the game has a chance to drop as Bloodied. Bloodied Items can also be acquired by earning Fresh Meat.

Even if none of that sounds exciting, you’re probably going to redownload the game for The Paladin free trial, which kicks off alongside the new season on March 11. The trial is only available until March 18, and it lets you try out the Paladin class.

The trial is available across PC, PlayStation, and Xbox. You’ll be able to take the new class for a spin, but your progress will be capped at level 25. The Paladin can be permanently unlocked by buying the Lord of Hatred expansion, as it’s one of two classes the expansion is introducing.

The good news is that any progress you make in the free trial will carry over to the full game if/when you buy the expansion.

Season of Slaughter also kicks off a Doom: The Dark Ages collaboration event. As we’ve come to expect, there’s a very limited free component to the collaboration, in the form of the Doom Reliquary. This is essentially a mini-battle pass that includes the Shield Saw skin, Slayer’s Flair, the head of the Cyberdemon as a back trophy and various other smaller bits.

The more impressive items - such as character skins, will instead be available to purchase for real money. The list includes the Doom Slayer armor, Mecha Dragon Serrat skin for your cat mount, and a Cacodemon pet.

Though the armor skin is cross-class compatible, judging by how much previous collaboration items have cost in Diablo 4, most of us probably won’t be spending that kind of money to get it.

#4314. Diablo 4’s Warlock looks like an unhinged Necromancer with Sorcerer energy in first look at gameplay

Diablo 4's practitioner of forbidden arts, The Warlock, has been officially unveiled as the second class coming with Lord of Hatred.

Thanks to a meaty, well-produced Diablo 4 Developer Update, we got to have our promised first look at gameplay of the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The showcase offered a deep look at the Warlock’s core archetypes, its gameplay and skills loop, and where the class sits within the game’s existing roster of diverse classes.

Since the initial reveal of Lord of Hatred, The Warlock has remained the mysterious second class. Anyone who pre-purchased the expansion was able to get immediate access to The Paladin, the other class arriving with the expansion. It wasn’t until February that Blizzard officially revealed the class to the world, but we had to wait until this most recent Developer Update to actually see it in action.

The Warlock’s pragmatism exists as the counterpart to The Paladin's purity, in that Warlocks don’t shy away from harnessing the powers of Hell to eliminate their enemies. The class can conjure up demons to do their bidding, and utilise attacks previously only available to legions of Hell.

The Warlock is a hybrid pet and caster class. Their gameplay revolves around summoning demons, and undermining enemies with shadow arts. They rely on two resources: Wrath, and Dominance. Casting Skills consumes Wrath, whereas Dominance is what allows the Warlock to summon and exploit demons.

The Warlock has four archetypes players can spec into. Legions are traditional summoners who rely on overwhelming numbers to crush enemies. Vanguards are closer to Sorcerers, capable of dealing damage head-on. Masterminds utilise shadowcraft to slowly drain their enemies. Finally, Ritualists are summoners of the most terrifying Hell demons.

The Warlock is able to do this by fusing Soul Shards into their bodies. Going down any of the four paths becomes available after reaching level 30, which is when the class mechanic is unlocked. Each Soul Shard is tied to a certain demon, and its through that power that the Warlock is able to call upon them in combat. Your choice does, of course, affect your abilities going forward.

Warlocks arrive alongside new Uniques that cater to their specific playstyles, which is similar to what we’ve previously seen with The Paladin, and The Spiritborn before that.

Lord of Hatred arrives April 28. While we wait, Diablo 4’s next season is kicking off next week to deliver a bit of mindless fun to hold us over until the big day.
